rules.title: Use lowercase for every name
Separate words with underscores, never at the start or end of a name
Keep special characters out of names
Spell names out in common terms, and abbreviate only with an approved acronym
Name a column for the fact it stores, not the action it asks for
Name columns in the positive voice
Name columns in the singular
Check what a numbered column name is really saying
A column named `id` is the table's bigint key, and `_id` points to one
A column named `guid` is a uuid, and `_guid` points to one
Use `identifier` for any identifying value that is neither an id nor a guid
A column that points at a row in the same database needs a real foreign key
A column ending in `_by` holds a user guid from identity_service
What a `_by` column holds when no user acted is an open decision
Make every column NOT NULL until you can say what a null in it would mean
Give a NOT NULL column a plan for the rows already in the table
Use a nullable boolean only when true, false, and unknown are all real answers
Use `date` for a day and `timestamptz` for a moment
If a date or timestamp name ends in a preposition, make it match the type
Never use `timestamp` without a time zone
Store timestamps in UTC and convert only for display
Use varchar, not char or text
Give every varchar the smallest limit your data honestly allows
Never go above varchar(65,535)
rules.second_opinion: DBA or Data Architect, before creating anything longer.

rules.title: Email addresses: varchar(254)
Store a URL in varchar(2048)
When data has no honest upper limit, decide on purpose where the limit lives
Never store a list of values as one delimited string
Treat a short text column as a fixed set unless there is a reason it is not
Have the database enforce a fixed set of values
Choose how to enforce a fixed set by asking what each value carries
Store a currency's code in `currency_code`
Never store money in float, real, or double
Store money as minor units in a bigint
Name each money column for what it holds, ending in `_minor_units`
Derive major units from minor units instead of storing a second copy
Never turn minor units into major units with a flat divide by 100
Calculate major units in a generated column with the standard block
Compute a value from other columns in the same row in the database, not in application code
When a value depends on how a row changed, let a trigger maintain it
Give almost every table `created_at` and `updated_at`, and let the database manage them
Keep `updated_at` current with the shared trigger, not with application code
Soft-delete rows by default, with a `deleted_at` timestamp, unless there is a reason not to
Change a row in place, and do not delete it and create it again
Name a table that joins two others for the two things it joins
Give every table an `id`, junction tables included, unless there is a stated reason not to
An `id` is an internal reference, so outside the database a row is found by its `guid`
Give a table a `guid` when something outside the database may point at its rows, and decide when the table is created
Make a `guid` NOT NULL and UNIQUE, and generate it wherever it is first needed
Before using an array column, check that it is not a second table you have not made
Do not keep a second copy of data that a view can derive
Start with a plain view, and move to a materialized view only when the query has earned it
When rows have the same shape whatever they belong to, keep one table and not one per parent

rules.title: Add an index when something looks the column up, in the same change that adds the lookup
Decide on purpose whether a foreign key column needs an index, because the database does not make one
Name a database in the singular, short and descriptive
Name a schema in the singular with no underscores
Use a schema where it divides a database into parts that mean something, and name it for what it holds
Do not name a schema after its own database
Name a primary key `pk_<table>` and a foreign key `fk_<table>_<column>`
Name every other constraint `ctx_<descriptor>`
Name every other index `idx_<table>_<column>`
Name a trigger `trg_<table>_<descriptor>`
Name a function `ufn_<descriptor>`
Name a stored procedure `usp_<descriptor>`
Name a view `uv_<table>_<descriptor>`
Name a materialized view `umv_<table>_<descriptor>`
Create a role with no login rights, named for what it covers and its access level
Name a user for the person or service it stands for, and describe a service account in its comment
